section_title: Economic Torts, Passing Off and Deceit

nodes.label: Economic Torts, Passing Off and Deceit
nodes.summary: Economic torts protecting business interests and trade: inducing breach of contract, conspiracy, intimidation, unlawful interference with trade, passing off, deceit/fraud, and malicious falsehood.

nodes.label: Economic Torts Overview
nodes.summary: Economic torts protect the claimant from intentional interference with their trade, business or economic interests. They generally require an intention to cause damage, as distinct from negligence causing pure economic loss.

nodes.label: Inducing Breach of Contract
nodes.summary: A person who knowingly and intentionally induces a party to breach a contract with the claimant is liable in tort. Requires: (1) knowledge of the contract, (2) intention to induce breach, (3) actual breach, (4) damage.

nodes.label: Conspiracy
nodes.summary: Two or more persons agree to do an unlawful act or a lawful act by unlawful means, causing damage to the claimant. Two forms: (1) conspiracy to injure (predominant purpose to cause damage), (2) unlawful means conspiracy.

nodes.label: Intimidation
nodes.summary: The defendant threatens an unlawful act against a third party, intending to cause the third party to act in a way that damages the claimant. The third party must comply (or be coerced) and the claimant must suffer loss.

nodes.label: Unlawful Interference with Trade
nodes.summary: A residual economic tort covering intentional interference with the claimant's trade or business by unlawful means. The defendant must intend to cause damage and use unlawful means against a third party that affects the claimant.

nodes.label: Passing Off Overview
nodes.summary: Passing off protects unregistered trade marks and business goodwill. Requires: (1) goodwill/reputation of the claimant, (2) misrepresentation by the defendant causing confusion, (3) damage to the claimant's goodwill.

nodes.label: Extended Passing Off (Advocat/Champagne)
nodes.summary: Extended passing off protects shared goodwill in a class of goods or services (e.g. champagne, Swiss watches). Requires distinctiveness of the class, misrepresentation as to membership, and damage to the class's goodwill.

nodes.label: Deceit / Fraud
nodes.summary: Deceit requires: (1) a false representation of fact made by the defendant, (2) knowledge of falsity or reckless indifference to truth, (3) intention that the claimant should act on it, (4) the claimant acts to their detriment.

nodes.label: Malicious Falsehood / Injurious Falsehood
nodes.summary: A false statement made maliciously (with spite or dominant motive to cause damage) about the claimant's goods, business or property, causing special damage. Differs from defamation in protecting property not reputation.

nodes.label: Defences to Economic Torts
nodes.summary: Justification (legitimate protection of interests), statutory authority, truth (for malicious falsehood), and absence of intention to cause damage. Competition law and market regulation may provide exemptions.
